- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.75) — model tends to overshoot early in the horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (e.g., <0.5) — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in price corrections — true drops often occur before forecasted troughs.
- After sharp price spikes, model overreacts and forecasts a prolonged rally — suppress peak forecasts if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- Mean reversion bias: model holds high forecasts longer than actual price reversion to mean — reduce forecasted values by 5–10% if sentiment shows cooling or divergence from recent highs.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early periods (e.g., 2025-01-28 to 2025-02-03) — adjust downward by 3–5% for first 5–7 days of forecast horizon if sentiment is stable or slightly positive.
